description: A creative team developing an interactive educational space exploration game for children.
summary: Ghosts Of Space is an educational game we have developed to make studying the space easier and funnier for children. During our research of NASA missions, we understood that many items of the equipment were left behind on the Moon and Mars. We found it fascinating to make a game where children could find these objects and know their histories. The players have to explore the Moon and Mars with the help of the robot. They will find the objects used during real NASA missions, learn about their usage, and perform tasks and questions. It was not only about creating a space game. The idea was to prove that even the equipment left behind can tell about space exploration. We wish that our game will encourage children to be interested in NASA, science, and space missions.
details:
Our project is called GHOSTS OF SPACE. Powered by NASA data, our project allows children to explore the Moon and Mars in a fun way. When players start the game, they are accompanied on their adventure by our robot. Together with the robot, we complete missions by examining important artifacts and evidence that NASA has left behind on the Moon and Mars. In this way, players learn what these objects were used for and why they are important. Interactive questions, mini-games, and various activities are designed to be both entertaining and educational.

We wanted to create something different from a standard educational program, and we achieved this by using our creativity. Rather than just giving information about space, we aimed to make players feel as if they are actually there. We made an effort to ensure the game is colorful, easy to understand, and suitable for younger players. Additionally, we restructured the learning process with diverse activities instead of repetitive tasks, and we included short videos to help players visualize the experience. During the development phase, we used platforms such as JavaScript, Codex, Suno (for our own custom-made music), and GitHub to build the game. As a team of two students, we combined our passion for space with our creativity.
